subject: VMWARE_ESXI_VIRTIO_CONTROLLED_ROUTE_PROFILE
scope: PCIe Correctable AER external behavior through public PCI configuration space, guest output and public ESXi logs; no VMware private-code reconstruction

safetyBoundary.precondition: Endpoint/root Correctable and Uncorrectable status is cleared and read back from a strict baseline before every injection
safetyBoundary.stopCondition: Any UES, non-CED Device Status or Root Uncorrectable reception delta pauses QEMU and stops the run
safetyBoundary.finalState: All registered ESXi cases restored the original 000 gate and closed the auxiliary Root path; outer QEMU was running and no active DirectPath user remained

gateModel.E: Endpoint PCIe Device Control Correctable Error Reporting Enable
gateModel.M: selected Endpoint Correctable Error Mask bit
gateModel.R: Root Error Command Correctable Error Reporting Enable

auxiliaryRootPathLease.note: The auxiliary Root path is managed separately from R and restored after every case

runs.interpretation: g100 injected and passed; g101 did not inject because only 14.611 seconds remained in the guest window versus the 15-second safety minimum. The aggregate is retained as harness history, not used to infer g101 behavior.

runs.parserBoundary: Guest event and counter parsing is corrected. The old host matcher labels SCP path audit lines as MATCH_OBSERVED; raw host deltas are reclassified below and are not treated as AER events.

runs.interpretation: Live smoke of the final guest and host semantic event parsers; both reported zero actual event lines.

qemuControl.endpointDeposition: All 64 rows deposited exactly the requested Endpoint CES/CED bit.
qemuControl.rootDeposition: Only E=1,M=0 rows g100 and g101 recorded Root COR_RCV; all E=0 or M=1 rows blocked Root deposition.
qemuControl.rootCommand: In the public QEMU 11.0.2 model, R controls Root notification eligibility and does not suppress Root status deposition after an ERR_COR message has arrived.
qemuControl.source: The Root Source readback matched requester 01:00.1; where the source was already 0x0101 at baseline, this establishes consistency rather than a source-register transition.

esxiIdle.claimScope: Frozen outer-QEMU fabric deposition plus ESXi post-resume black-box observation; not ESXi service or interrupt attribution

esxiActive.g100: PASS with the final guest and host parsers
esxiActive.g101: PASS; raw host audit lines were reclassified as collection noise

profileComparison.historicalE1000e: AER header hidden in the guest while raw status was projected; Endpoint/Root CERE and Root COR_EN were disabled.
profileComparison.controlledVirtio: AER capability and raw CES were visible in the active guest, while Linux AER counters did not increase and no kernel AER event was observed.
profileComparison.conclusion: Guest capability visibility, raw status projection and guest service/event delivery are independent observable surfaces.

observedBehavior.boundedLogs: After excluding SCP audit paths, collection markers and grep-process noise, no semantic AER/PCI error event was observed in the captured host or guest windows. This does not prove that ESXi performed no internal service.

externalBehaviorModel: Endpoint Correctable status deposition is independent from Root message deposition.
For the QEMU-controlled fabric, E=1 and M=0 are required for Root deposition; R is a separate Root notification-eligibility dimension.
The frozen Root snapshots establish QEMU fabric behavior under gates observable as programmed by ESXi, not VMware's private service algorithm.
ESXi DirectPath guest AER capability visibility is profile-dependent in the tested build.
A visible AER capability and raw CES transition do not by themselves constitute Linux guest AER service/event delivery.
Bounded host-log absence cannot identify or exclude an ESXi interrupt or service path.

parserCorrections.guest: Old active-v2 output counted aer_dev_correctable/fatal/nonfatal sysfs section labels as events. Raw logs show TOTAL_ERR_COR/FATAL/NONFATAL stayed zero and no PCIe Bus Error or semantic severity event occurred.
parserCorrections.host: Old output matched aer-correctable in SCP audit paths and Replay inside a collection-process name. The final parser excludes collection audit records and uses semantic PCI/AER terms.
parserCorrections.validation: The executed final-parser hash passed self-tests and the live g100 active smoke. The current runner additionally passes a fail-closed self-test proving that an unsafe pre-write baseline leaves QEMU paused.

runnerHashes.postRunSafetyChange: The current runner differs from the executed g100 hash only by fail-closed unsafe-pre-write baseline handling and its self-test; no behavioral result was re-attributed to the new hash.

claimsExcluded: ESXi interrupt, Root service or notification-path attribution
An inference of no ESXi internal service from bounded log absence
Guest write isolation for the visible or hidden AER body
Root W1C repeat, re-arm and multiple-message lifecycle behavior
Physical-link error generation or physical device recovery
Reset cleanliness, health, quarantine or safe tenant reuse
Other ESXi builds, devices, firmware, guest profiles or Qman product conformance
limitations: Only Receiver Error was exercised across all eight ESXi E/M/R gates; all eight Correctable bits were covered only by the QEMU public-model control.
Active g100 and g101 are single successful observations, not the required three-run repeatability matrix.
R=0 and R=1 produced the same frozen Root deposition, but no observation identifies the resulting ESXi interrupt or service behavior.
The raw run directories are external sibling artifacts and are not committed to this repository; their result and manifest digests are pinned here.
The observation is limited to one nested q35/OVMF ESXi build and one synthetic virtio endpoint.
